summary: Intermittent streaming timeouts due to stale POP affinity cache causing 'hot-potato' inter-region routing
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC NordicFin (enterprise) reported elevated p95/p99 inference latency and intermittent streaming cancellations for chat endpoints. Impact: Customer observed client-side 504s and stalled streaming chunks; tail latency increased from baseline p99 ~800ms to >6s for some requests. Scope: Reported for customers with EU POP affinity but observed traces showing sudden handoffs to US POPs during request lifetime. Environment: prod eu-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use customer's API key and call /v1/chat with streaming=true from eu-west; 2) Issue a long multi-turn prompt (~600 tokens); 3) Observe first chunks arrive then long pause (3-10s) before resume or cancellation. Observed behavior: - Traces show initial connection to eu-west-edge-03, after 1-2 tokens traffic is forwarded to us-east-edge-01 (TTL ~20s) - TCP connection is reused at proxy layer without full reconnect leading to head-of-line blocking on the forwarding path - Kernel tcp retransmit counters spike on proxy host. Logs: "proxy=eu-west-edge-03 forward=us-east-edge-01 route_cache=stale pop_affinity_cache_age=128s conn_reuse=1". Metrics: - p50 unchanged, p95 up 300-900ms, p99 up to 6-8s for affected time windows - 504s correlated with abrupt route handover windows - Flow logs (vpc-flow) show small bursts of inter-region egress during incidents. Initial hypothesis: A stale POP-affinity cache in the regional proxy layer persisted past a routing failover; the proxy tries to preserve connections by reusing upstream sockets, forwarding to a remote POP resulting in extra RTT and occasional packet loss leading to stalls/timeouts. Investigation notes: - SRE captured tcpdump of a reproduced case and saw FIN/ACKs from upstream followed by retransmit backlog - Edge proxy config shows cache TTL misaligned with global route-change TTL (edge TTL = 120s, control-plane route TTL = 30s) - Early mitigation: rolled back cache TTL change on eu-west-edge fleet and enabled strict upstream reconfirmation for active streaming sessions (hotfix rolled at 2026-03-11 05:30 UTC). Current state: Hotfix reduced incidents but not fully resolved; working on a coordinated control-plane cache invalidation mechanism and test coverage for streaming handoff. Next steps: 1) Implement cache invalidation push (infra) and force refresh for all eu-west-edge (sprint P0) 2) Add E2E test that simulates route flapping during active streaming 3) Monitor for 72 hours and coordinate with NordicFin CS to validate. Runbooks/links: incident runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-03-10-27, grafana traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/latency-overview?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west
